meta.question: Replace the threshold-free direct-SSB limit (P=1) with the rigorous Nikjoo/Charlton energy-threshold ramp on the per-event deposited energy. What does the parameter-free direct model then predict?
meta.method: Shaders now emit per-event deposited energy (rad_e buffer, new binding); direct scorer breaks with P(E)=clamp((E-E_low)/(E_high-E_low),0,1). Fresh GPU dump (Phase A+B) + Node IRT + SSB scoring, N=4096/10 keV.

finding: The rigorous per-event energy-threshold model predicts indirect/direct = 6.5, ABOVE PARTRAC's 2-3 band. Diagnosis (not a bug): the mean deposit at an in-reach ionisation is ~15 eV, giving ramp P~0.31, so only ~1/3 of near-backbone ionisations break. A single water ionisation rarely deposits >37.5 eV. The per-event threshold under-counts direct SSB vs the ACCUMULATED-volume energy that PARTRAC/Nikjoo integrate (overlapping deposits summed in the sugar-phosphate volume). Both the ramp and the P=1 limit are parameter-free; the 2.32 vs 6.5 span measures direct-SSB sensitivity to sub-threshold accounting.
followup: Accumulate deposited energy per sugar-phosphate voxel across events, then threshold once (true Nikjoo/Charlton model), instead of the per-event proxy.
status: pass (implemented + GPU-validated); honest-negative on the ratio — parameter-free prediction lands above PARTRAC's band
